headline: Google Puts Agents Behind Its MCP Gate
lede: Google will require Workspace agents to pass through its MCP servers, adding quotas, retention limits, and partner-only capabilities. The Gmail connector can read and draft—but not send, reply, forward, or edit—leaving developers to weigh safety controls against a narrower, more centralized interface.

headline: Intel Ships a Mono Font for Clearer Code
lede: Intel One Mono is an open-source typeface built around legibility in the terminal and editor. Its four weights, broad Latin coverage, screen-tuned builds, and accessibility-informed glyph design make the case in the only language that matters here: readable characters.

headline: When Machines Start Doing Mathematics
lede: A satirical dispatch imagines AI labs solving some of mathematics’ most famous open problems, from circuit lower bounds to the Riemann Hypothesis. Beneath the exaggeration lies a serious question about machine-assisted proof—and how quickly excitement outruns independent verification.
pullquote: The hard part is no longer imagining machine-made mathematics; it is knowing which results deserve belief.

headline: 1Password Reports a Backend Security Incident
lede: An attacker used a compromised employee GitHub account to reach private source code and CI/CD systems. 1Password says vault contents, passwords, and encryption keys remained protected, but customer metadata and certain invitation or recovery tokens were exposed.

headline: The Unix Commentary That Traveled Underground
lede: John Lions’s explanation of Unix Version 6 kernel source became indispensable precisely because it could not be distributed openly. For two decades, students copied it by hand and circulation; its eventual publication preserved one of computing’s clearest paths into operating-system design.

headline: Moat Bundles Model Access for Five Dollars
lede: Moat offers a unified API to several AI models for a $5 monthly membership, with token usage billed at stated wholesale-style rates. The proposition is clean: pooled demand, fewer provider decisions, and cheaper access—subject to the usual questions about reliability, privacy, and durable pricing.

headline: The Times Tells Photographers to Skip Photoshop
lede: The New York Times is warning freelance photographers away from Photoshop 2027 and later, whose AI features may attach provenance metadata to assignment images. The policy protects a strict editorial record, while Adobe’s unclear feature triggers leave ordinary editing workflows under suspicion.

headline: A Shorter Lean Formalization of the GRH
lede: Anthropic collaborators have released compact Lean 4 formalizations of the Riemann and Generalized Riemann Hypotheses, reducing one version to roughly 76,000 lines. The artifact is machine-checkable and reproducible, though its authors distinguish formal verification from mathematical review or explanatory understanding.

headline: Minipg Turns PostgreSQL Into One Executable
lede: Minipg packages PostgreSQL, its configuration, credentials, and data directory into a portable `.pgdb` bundle. A Zig-based Linux personality handles the runtime without Docker or a full virtual machine; the trade is early-stage performance and a warning to keep irreplaceable data elsewhere.

headline: Sixty-Nine Guides Map Interface History
lede: This collection preserves 69 interface style guides from the early 1980s to the present, spanning Amiga, Macintosh, Unix, Palm, iOS, Android, and webOS. Together they show how widgets, conventions, and design systems moved from local documentation into the shared grammar of modern software.
